newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rebound, seen down slightly.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rebound, seen down slightly.

text.p: Polish shares rose after a three -session fall but analysts said the market was likely to ease again tomorrow amid macroeconomic and election uncertainties.

Poland's parliamentary elections are due on September 21 while expected government borrowing from the central bank to pay for flood damage has heightened concerns of higher deficits, inflation and rates which would limit share-buying.

"(Tuesday's) data that broad money rose (2.8 percent in July's first 10 days) not considering money from loans given to the government is a factor suggesting we can have an inflation wave," said Roman Sosnowski of WBK-AIB Asset Management.

Analysts said Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's upbeat Tuesday report on the U.S. economy would have little effect on Polish shares as the small investors who sometimes speculate on such information were pre-occupied with several domestic factors.
They said one such domestic factor was Tuesday's news the Securities Commission (KPW) notified the public prosecutor that a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices.
Garment maker Prochnik fell 10 percent on speculation it might have been among stocks illegally manipulated, analysts said.
The main WIG index rose 0.4 percent to 15,189.0 and turnover fell 11.4 percent to 145.8 million zlotys ($42.4 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 44 to 37 with 25 stocks flat.
Analysts said it was suspected that largely parallel market prices were the subject of possible price manipulation and that main market sentiment would likely not be hurt by the news.
They said edible fats maker Kruszwica jumped 6.3 percent after Tuesday's news the Cereol unit of French-Italian Eridania Beghin-Say agreed to buy a 45 percent stake.
